runs.question: How does the NIST Generative AI Profile describe data privacy risks?

answer.text:
The NIST Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) treats data privacy as one of its 12 named GAI risks. I was not able to read its detailed discussion of that risk. The search tool failed, so I read the front sections directly.

**Definition:** The profile frames data privacy as a risk of harm from exposed personal information. It covers impacts due to leakage and unauthorized use, disclosure, or de-anonymization of biometric, health, location, or other personally identifiable information or sensitive data. It also notes that what is categorized as sensitive data or sensitive PII can be highly contextual based on the nature of the information, with examples including political opinions, sex life, or criminal convictions.

**Where it sits in the risk taxonomy:** The profile places data privacy in more than one category. It lists it under misuse by humans (or malicious use) and under ecosystem / societal risks (or systemic risks), and it also appears among technical/model risks. The profile adds that some risks are cross-cutting between these categories.

**Mapping:** Each risk is linked to the AI RMF's trustworthy AI characteristics, in Section 3 (as well as in tables in Appendix B). I did not read Section 3 or the suggested actions, so I can't say what mitigations the profile recommends for privacy.
